Continuous Curve

CurvesGeometryParadoxes
Game: Watch one line spiral inward and look at how it tricks your eye into seeing squares stacked inside squares.
How to play: Move the three sliders to change the gap around the line, the step between turns and the number of straight pieces. Drag the dot onto the line, or focus it and press the arrow keys to follow the line piece by piece.
Look for the math

The picture looks like a set of squares inside squares. It is really one spiral drawn without lifting the pen. The old applet drew it with exactly three controls; this page keeps their ranges and their starting values.

One line, no lifts

The applet's drawing loop stores a pen position and a side length. Each step works out one new corner, draws a straight leg to it and then makes that corner the pen position. The result is a polyline: leg i + 1 always begins where leg i ended. The logic test checked this over 341,979 settings — there is not a single gap or separate square in the drawing.

How the corners move inward

The first side is min(width, height) − 15 − 2 × Edge gap, and the pen starts at ((width − side)/2, (height − side)/2), with integer division as in the Java code. The directions repeat down, right, up, left. After the very first right-hand leg, the side shrinks by Turn step on the second and fourth leg of each lap. So after every four legs the next corner has moved in by exactly Turn step in both directions. The test compared every value of all three sliders (0–100, 2–34 and 4–100) with a second transcription of the applet's bytecode, plus several canvas shapes, and found no difference.

The squares are in your eye

The page says the tendency is to see embedded squares, and the picture's caption says there are no squares, only a continuous spiral. Both are right in different ways. Each lap is almost a square, but its last leg stops short by Turn step and the next lap starts one step inward: the path never closes. This is an optical illusion about how the eye groups shapes, not a claim that the drawing contains separate squares.

Put Turn step at 2 and Straight pieces at 100, then use the arrow keys to follow the dot. Try to keep your eye on the dot rather than on the shapes around it.
